## 0. Scope, Mission Framing, and Reading Rules

### 0.1 What this volume owns
| Finding | This volume delivers | |---|---| | F-005 | Versioned configuration schemas (§1), validation/default/absence semantics, precedence + effective readback, per-field change authority and activation, manager-creation setting, per-agent capability/approval config, composition of project instructions + base role + named specialization | | F-013 | Report schema with correlation, trusted timestamps, outcome vocabulary, acceptance layering, criteria provenance/versioning, waiting states, delivery semantics (§3) | | F-014 | Deployment startup readiness, dependency failure, transport checks, restore ordering, queued-work recovery, crier-bridge lifecycle (§5) | | F-015 | Metric register, counter scopes/windows/resets, cheaper-unchanged-cycle measurement, the provisional 8-cycle calculation, requirement-to-test traceability, end-to-end acceptance scenarios (§4) | | F-016/17/18 | Precise redraw specifications for figures 2.1-1, 2.3-1, 2.1-2, 2.2-1, 2.2-2, 2.3-2, 2.4-1 (§7) |

### 0.2 Mission framing (review-log `mission`)
The reviewed mission is: *"A general-purpose hierarchy accepts ongoing VP direction, decomposes objectives, builds and equips teams, and coordinates director → managers → supervisors → foremen/workers until the requested outcome is delivered; coding is one application, not the limit."*
Consequences for this volume:
- **Configuration is domain-neutral.** Nothing in §1 names a coding-only tool, skill, or artifact type. `artifacts` in reports are opaque verifiable references (§3.1); the email-manager example of D-002 must be expressible with the same schema as a fleet-ops manager. - **Ongoing direction.** VP configuration (§1.3) is the standing layer that survives across objectives; acceptance criteria (§3.6) attach per assignment. Both layers exist precisely because direction is continuous. - **Building and equipping teams** is a configured capability (`manager_creation`, `create_subordinate`, `grantable_pool`), not a hard-coded org chart (§1.4–§1.5).

### 0.3 Deferred scope (review-log `deferred_scope` — binding)
Sophisticated dynamic model-routing algorithms and numerical tuning of concurrency limits are OUT of scope. This volume specifies configuration fields, pass-through boundaries, and queue semantics only (§1.6, §4). Where DESIGN.md shows numeric defaults (e.g. `verify.deadline_s` 1800, `max_fanout` 12, `max_inflight` 4/2), those are retained as owner-confirmed values from the normative source — they are configuration semantics, not tuning.

### 0.4 Requirement conventions
- **VOLD-nnn** — normative requirement of this volume. - **OPEN-VOLD-n** — a point the review explicitly left open. It MUST be resolved by design work or owner ruling before the affected field ships; it is never resolved by an undocumented default. - SHALL/MUST/ MAY per RFC 2119. "VP config" means the operator/VP-owned configuration layer (harness.toml and its validated write path, CT-01, R-001).
---
## PART I — CONFIGURATION AND SESSION POLICY
## 1. Configuration Depth (F-005)

### 1.2 Validation, default, and absence semantics
- **VOLD-003** — Every v3/v4 field has exactly one disposition class: 1. **REQUIRED-EXPLICIT** — absence is a load error. Used for every field where the review left the default open or where a silent default would be dangerous: `hierarchy.manager_creation.enabled`, `capability.create_subordinate`, `approval.*`, `runtime.provider`, `runtime.model`, `runtime.context_window`, `composition.base_role`, `specialization.authorized_overrides`, `hermesBinding.*`. 2. **EXPLICIT-DEFAULT** — a default exists in the normative source (DESIGN.md or contracts v1/v2) and is printed by the effective readback whenever it applies: `verify.deadline_s` (1800), `verify.remind_gap_s` (300), `verify.max_reminds` (2), `orchestration.max_fanout` (12), `orchestration.stale_after_s` (2× cycle; template value 7200), gateway `max_inflight` (4 main / 2 remote per Table 2.1-1), `session.reuse_policy` (`reuse-until-wedged`). 3. **REQUIRED** with no default and no open question — the v2 set (ids, bindings, rooms, workdir, skills). No field may carry a default that neither the review nor DESIGN.md confirms (F-005 completion rule: "Do not invent an unconfirmed default").
- **VOLD-004** — Validation order is: schema (types/patterns/enums) → referential integrity (gateway ids exist; room participants exist; registry entries exist for every agent with `responsibility`; grant tools exist in the tool universe) → policy (grant-vs-include consistency per VOLD-003 note; specialization override authorization per VOLD-015; precedence conflicts per VOLD-006) → warnings (e.g. a manager with `triggers: []` and `max_parallel.task: 0` can never be woken for work — legal but flagged). All errors carry `{code, json_path, detail}` and the loader fails closed on any error.

### 1.3 Precedence and effective readback (D-016, D-008)
Authority layers, highest wins:
1. **VP configuration** — operator/VP-owned harness.toml grants, limits, roles, approvals. VP-configured permissions are already granted; they require no director grant (D-016). 2. **Director on-demand delegation** — changes the director is authorized to make within its delegatable authority (grants from its `grantable_pool`, reassignment, criteria extension). Recorded with provenance `{origin: director, granted_by, granted_at, authority_ref}` where `authority_ref` names the VP-configured grant-authority record that permits it. 3. **Specialization overrides** — only those listed in `specialization.authorized_overrides` (VOLD-015). 4. **Base role template** — defaults nothing wins over 1–3.
- **VOLD-005** — On conflict between layers 1 and any lower layer, VP configuration wins and the harness records a `grant_conflict` audit event naming both sources. The losing value is never applied, not even advisory. Instruction-layer conflicts and permission-layer conflicts are distinguished (D-016 scope): permission conflicts are hard-checked at load and at grant time; instruction conflicts are handled per VOLD-014. - **VOLD-006 (effective readback)** — The harness exposes `GET /v1/effective-config/{agent-id}` (new endpoint, VP-only per the ENDPOINTS actor matrix) returning the fully resolved per-agent configuration: every field with its value, **provenance** (`vp | director | base | specialization`), the source reference (config path + line, or grant record id), and a `config_digest` (hash of the resolved document). Readback is the authoritative artifact for audits and for the acceptance scenarios of §4.4; an enforcement decision that cannot be reproduced from readback is a defect.
Readback has two scopes and they must agree: **config-scope** (current VP resolution, the endpoint above) and **session-scope** (`GET /v1/policy/effective?session=<bond-id>`, VOL-C §8.7): the session form returns the frozen `SessionPolicySnapshot` contents and its `policy_rev`, and MUST equal the snapshot byte-for-byte (digest comparison, VOLC-068b). A divergence is a §6 integrity defect, never a cache miss. Both forms report the four permission classes separately (`use`, `grant`, `confer_delegation`, `create`) so a grantor-without-use configuration reads back as exactly that rather than as a single opaque "allowed" list (VOLD-011).

### 1.4 Who may change each field, and when updates activate
- **VOLD-007 (change authority)** — Per field class:
| Field class | May change | Mechanism | |---|---|---| | Roles, room membership, gateway bindings, limits/caps, clocks (triggers), manager_creation, approval policy | Operator/VP only | harness.toml via the validated loader path (CT-01, R-001, N-2); agents have no write surface (DESIGN.md §6.3) | | On-demand grants from its `grantable_pool` | Director (and any agent configured `grantable_pool` non-empty, per D-009) | grant API call, recorded with provenance; bounded by VP-authorized pool and `authority_ref` | | Specialization content | Operator/VP (skill assets); director may request, never write | config path only | | Acceptance criteria per assignment | Director within D-010 (derive/extend); VP-supplied criteria are VP-owned | assignment record (§3.6) | | Anything else | No one at runtime | — |
An agent editing its own binding, skills, grants, or membership is a §6 integrity violation (DESIGN §6.3); the harness write gate rejects it and the attempt is counted.
- **VOLD-008 (activation timing)** — Config changes activate at the earliest of these well-defined points, never mid-request. For D-038, `session.fork_policy` and `session.resync` activation affects only future fork/resync authorization boundaries; it never rewrites an existing snapshot. At activation, reads and writes already authorized continue under their captured revision; a grant issuance already admitted completes only for its current request and new issuance is checked against current authority. - **Immediately at next orchestrator check**: caps, limits, room membership (router reads current config at wake-composition time). - **Next scheduler registration pass**: trigger/cron changes (re-registered through CT-02's validated path). - **Session boundary**: skills, tools, model/context, approval policy — applied at the next NEW session, or at the next REUSE turn (i.e. the next message delivered into the bonded session). Hermes owns within-session behavior; CHD does not mutate a live turn (hermes_gateway_check: profile routing and session continuation are Hermes contracts). In-flight sends complete under the configuration they were dispatched with; the send manifest records the `config_digest` at dispatch (§3.3), which is what verification uses. - VP-grant **revocation** is resolved at the snapshot boundary, never lazily on a later request: use rights already resolved into a session's effective-policy snapshot continue for the life of that session (VOL-C §8.9 VOLC-069), and sessions created after the revocation resolve without the revoked grant (R6/R7). Issuing any **new** downstream grant is blocked at once (a director delegation citing a revoked `authority_ref` fails `403 authority_revoked`), and archive reads re-check every page (VOLC-072b).

### 1.5 Manager creation (D-005)
- **VOLD-009** — `hierarchy.manager_creation.enabled` is REQUIRED-EXPLICIT (VOLD-003): the document is invalid without it. This satisfies "do not invent an unconfirmed default" by making omission impossible rather than by guessing the owner's intent. - **Disabled case:** a director request to create a manager is refused `403 manager_creation_disabled`, counted (`manager_creation_refused_total`), and surfaced to the VP in the director's next report — the blocked-work path of D-009/Q-004 (report upward) is the only fallback. - **Enabled case:** creation is bounded by `max_director_created` (counted, enforced), uses the named `role_template` for base composition, binds to a gateway from `gateway_pool`, and — the hard constraint — token provisioning is `token_provisioning: "operator"`: role tokens are operator-provisioned files (DESIGN FACT-20, §6.3). A director-created manager is therefore **provisioned pending operator token grant**; the director's creation request produces a provisioning record and the manager is not dispatchable until the operator completes token provisioning. This is a constraint inherited from the platform, not a policy choice, and is recorded as such in the provisioning record. - Every creation, enable, disable, and refusal is audited (`/chd/audit` event, harness-written). - **VOLD-010** — Lower-tier creation (`create_subordinate`) is modeled by the same enum (`none | supervisor | manager`); the foreman/worker scope remains OPEN (OPEN-VOLD-2) and the enum MUST NOT be extended to `foreman`/`worker` until the F-002 owner decision lands.

### 1.6 Per-agent capability, approval, and instance binding (D-008, D-009)
- **VOLD-011 (four distinct permission classes, not three)** — `capability` models **use**, **grant use**, **confer delegation** and **create** independently. In `contracts/config.schema.json` the first three are `permissions.use`, `permissions.grant` and `permissions.confer_delegation` (each with `capabilities`, `resource_scope`, `recipients`, `limits`); `create` stays on `create_subordinate` (VOLD-010). No class is inferred from another: an agent with `permissions.grant.capabilities: ["telegram.send"]` and no `permissions.use` entry may authorize a *subordinate* to send via Telegram while being unable to send itself (the D-009 grantor case); an agent with `grant` but no `confer_delegation` may hand out use-rights but may not mint another grantor (D-032). Both are required validation-valid configurations (worked example §1.8; decision table VOL-C §8.3.1 rows 2–3). Legacy key names (`grants`, `grantable_pool`) remain accepted as the v2/v3 spelling of `permissions.use.capabilities` / `permissions.grant.capabilities` and are refused if both spellings appear (`permission_key_conflict`, VOLC-068c). - **VOLD-012 (goal assignment ≠ permission grant)** — Assignment messages (`kind: task|directive`, §3.1) carry completion conditions and context only. The messaging write path MUST reject any assignment whose payload attempts to mutate `capability`, `approval`, rooms, or skills (`403 assignment_not_grant`); grant records are created exclusively by (a) the config path or (b) an authorized grant API call with provenance. Skill or prompt text claiming an authority is not an effective grant (F-012) — enforcement is the write gate, not wording. - **VOLD-013 (approval policy per agent)** — `approvals.human_approval_required` plus `approvals.gates` (action classes requiring human approval, e.g. `"send-external"`, `"payment"`, `"delete"`) are configured per agent (D-008). There is no universal approval policy and no default; the per-assignment completion/approval condition of Q-006 layers on top of this (§3.8). Approval-gated actions that proceed without the recorded human approval are integrity violations counted and paged (§4.1). - **VOLD-014 (instances and profiles)** — Agents may be separate profiles on one Hermes instance or on different instances (D-008): `hermesBinding.instance` must reference an existing gateway id (the gateway row carries url/transport/auth per DATA-MODEL §1.2), and `hermesBinding.profile` names the Hermes profile. Per the hermes_gateway_check, named profile routing binds authentication to the routed profile; CHD therefore MUST map each agent to a distinct profile (two agents sharing one profile is a validation error `profile_shared`) so that per-agent credentials and tool policy are attributable. CHD does not reimplement profile or session mechanics; it selects among documented Hermes REST session operations (create/continue/history/forks) per the NEW/REUSE mapping owned by VOL-C (F-010) — this volume only pins that `runtime.*` values ride the delivery payload (VOLD-015).

### 1.7 Provider/model/context pass-through (D-015)
- **VOLD-015** — `runtime.{provider, model, context_window, max_turns, token_budget}` are passed verbatim to the Hermes gateway POST (the transport of FACT-11 already carries model/provider). CHD owns selection and delivery; **Hermes owns fallback**. CHD MUST NOT retry a failed delivery with a different model or provider, MUST NOT maintain a model-health table, and MUST NOT interpret a provider outage as authorization to reroute (deferred_scope; D-015). Fallback behavior is observable only: session metadata (as reported by Hermes) is recorded in the send manifest for readback. No routing algorithms are specified here or elsewhere (deferred_scope). - **VOLD-016** — `context_window` is a configured ceiling CHD passes through; CHD does not compute context budgets, compact, or reconstruct history (R-019). Context lives in the room log; agents read it themselves.

### 1.8 Composition: project instructions + base role + named specialization (D-015, D-016, Q-008)
- **VOLD-017 (order)** — The instruction/skill composition order is: 1. **Project instructions** — Hermes-native project/workspace instruction files in the agent's `workdir` (Hermes-owned reading; CHD only sets the workdir and `composition.project_scope` list of additional workspace roots). 2. **Base role template** — `composition.base_role` (the role skill, e.g. the manager base; naming examples are provisional per D-015). 3. **Named specialization** — `composition.specialization.name` (e.g. an email-collection manager specialization). Later layers refine earlier ones. CHD composes the *list* and delivers it; Hermes composes the *behavior*. - **VOLD-018 (conflict handling)** — Two conflict planes: - **Permissions (hard):** a specialization's grants/overrides apply only within `authorized_overrides` (VOLD-019); anything else loses to base and VP layers per VOLD-005. - **Instructions (best-effort, explicit):** where specialization text contradicts base-role text and `behavior` is NOT in `authorized_overrides`, the loader fails validation (`specialization_conflict`) — CHD does not silently pick a winner in prose it cannot enforce. Where `behavior` IS authorized, the specialization wins over base (never over VP config) and the effective readback shows the override with its authorization record (Q-008: overrides allowed when authorized by VP config or valid on-demand director delegation; VP config prevails). - **VOLD-019 (specialization override authorization)** — `specialization.authorized_overrides ⊆ {behavior, permissions}` is REQUIRED-EXPLICIT (empty list = specialize-only, the conservative legal default *of the enumeration*, not an invented behavioral default). `permissions` overrides must additionally name the exact grant deltas in the specialization asset; the loader verifies each named delta lies within the VP-configured `grantable_pool` of the agent (D-016: specialization may override base permissions "when authorized"; authorization cannot exceed the VP pool). - **VOLD-020 (scope)** — `composition.project_scope` supports multiple project/workspace roots per agent (D-015 "support multiple project/workspace scopes"). Scope entries are absolute paths validated to exist at load; CHD does not merge file contents — Hermes does. - **VOLD-021 (temporary agents)** — Defaults for temporary/ephemeral agents are NOT SETTLED (D-015: "exact defaults not settled"). **OPEN-VOLD-1.** Until resolved, temporary agents are unsupported: the schema has no `temporary: true` flag, and any mechanism that would create one fails validation `temporary_agents_unspecified`. This is the honest encoding of the open point; it is reopened by an owner ruling, not by an implementer.

### 1.9 Worked configuration examples (F-005 completion evidence)
**Valid — grantor who cannot use what it grants (D-009):**
```yaml - id: mgr-comms role: manager gateway: gw-main capability: grants: # USE - {tool: room.post, scope: "obj-*", origin: vp} - {tool: room.read, scope: "obj-*", origin: vp} grantable_pool: # GRANT (superset of own use) - telegram.send - artifact.deliver create_subordinate: supervisor approval: human_approval_required: false gates: [] composition: base_role: chd-manager-base # provisional naming (D-015) specialization: name: outbound-comms authorized_overrides: [] # specialize-only runtime: provider: fireworks model: accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3-flash context_window: 160000 ```
Load outcome: valid. `mgr-comms` may grant `telegram.send` to a supervisor; `mgr-comms` itself has no `telegram.send` use grant; an attempt by mgr-comms to send via Telegram fails at the service boundary `403 tool_not_granted`.
**Invalid cases and specified outcomes:**
| Invalid document | Error | Outcome | |---|---|---| | Tool in `tools.include` with no matching grant | `tool_without_grant` | load refused | | `hierarchy` block absent | `required_missing{path: hierarchy}` | load refused | | `manager_creation.enabled` absent | `required_missing` | load refused (VOLD-009) | | Specialization overrides `permissions` not in `authorized_overrides` | `specialization_conflict` | load refused (VOLD-018) | | Specialization permission delta beyond the agent's VP pool | `override_exceeds_pool` | load refused (VOLD-019) | | Two agents share one `hermesBinding.profile` on one instance | `profile_shared` | load refused (VOLD-014) | | Director delegation granting outside its `grantable_pool` | `403 grant_outside_pool` at grant time | refused, audited, counted | | VP-config grant vs director delegation for the same tool+scope | VP wins + `grant_conflict` audit event | VOLD-005 | | Manager-creation request while disabled | `403 manager_creation_disabled` | refused, counted (VOLD-009) |

### 1.10 Storage classes and routing configuration (R31-028, D-034)
The deployment MUST treat storage as four logical data classes, not as one undifferentiated DuckBrain target. The controller remains the default authority; local or federated project memory is an allowed extension, not a requirement.
| Data class | Authoritative backend | Sync mode | Acknowledgement rule | Effective readback field | |---|---|---|---|---| | `coordination_report` | controller DuckBrain, `/chd` | immediate | `controller_fsync`; a locally queued write is **not** completion | `coordination_report.backend` | | `control_key` | controller DuckBrain, `/chd` | immediate | `controller_fsync`; no local fallback | `control_key.backend` | | `session_archive` | controller archive ingestor, `/chd-archive` | checkpointed | `committed_checkpoint` before advertisement | `session_archive.backend` | | `project_code_memory` | deployment-selected controller, local, or federated store; optional | background or disabled | `local_enqueue_not_complete`; eventual lag is visible | `project_code_memory.backend` |
```json "storage": { "classes": { "coordination_report": {"namespace":"chd","backend":"controller","sync":"immediate"}, "control_key": {"namespace":"chd","backend":"controller","sync":"immediate"}, "session_archive": {"namespace":"chd-archive","backend":"controller","sync":"checkpointed"}, "project_code_memory": {"namespace":null,"backend":"none | controller | local | federated","sync":"background | disabled"} }, "controller": {"backend_url":"https://...","auth_token_ref":"..."}, "effective_readback": "/v1/effective-routing" } ```
The checked-in template is topology **T-A central-default**: control/report and archive are controller-authoritative, and optional project memory is disabled. Topology **T-B central + local/federated project memory** is a supported deployment variant: set only `project_code_memory` to `local` or `federated`, give it an explicit namespace and grant, and retain a controller proxy plus background sync. Neither topology requires per-host DuckBrain, and local project memory is not rejected.
- **VOLD-056.** `coordination_report` and `control_key` MUST be `controller` with `immediate` sync. A report/control write MUST NOT be acknowledged from a local queue, delayed sync, or project-memory write. If the controller is unavailable, the named failure is `503 control_store_unavailable`; the item remains queued or `blocked` and no completion/verdict is manufactured. `session_archive` MUST be a distinct namespace from control. `project_code_memory` may be local/federated, with background sync, but may not receive a report or control write. - **VOLD-057.** Per-tool routing is explicit in `storage.tool_class`. A tool whose class is coordination/report or control executes against the controller. Effective readback at `GET /v1/effective-routing` returns, for all four classes, `{backend, namespace, sync, proxy, credential_ref_name, digest}` plus `last_synced_rev/ts` for project memory. Credential refs are names only. - **VOLD-058.** Background sync has a named `sync_owner`, an explicit conflict rule, checkpoint `last_synced_rev/ts`, and observable lag. Default conflict behavior is `controller_wins` for central keys and `local_wins_on_project_keys` for project-only keys. Sync ownership is single-writer per namespace; conflicts are recorded and retried from the checkpoint, never silently dropped. - **VOLD-059.** Access grants are per class and endpoint: controller authorization does not authorize a project-memory backend. Every read/write audit records the class, backend, principal, grant id, checkpoint, and outcome.

### 1.11 Session fork policy (D-038, R31-027)
```json "session": { "fork_policy": "preserve_parent_snapshot", // default "resync": { "enabled": false, "authorized_by": ["session_policy_authority", "session.policy_resync"], "requires_approval": false }, "per_agent_override": { "mgr-infra": "current_policy" }, "per_project_override": { "proj-a": "preserve_parent_snapshot" } } ```
- **VOLD-060.** `session.fork_policy` is one of `preserve_parent_snapshot | current_policy`, with schema default `preserve_parent_snapshot` printed in readback. `session.resync.enabled` defaults to `false` (off); unknown fork modes are rejected. Scope: global default, per-agent override, per-project override; an override may narrow (be stricter) but MUST NOT widen the VP setting (`fork_policy_widen_refused`). - **VOLD-061.** Activation is at fork creation and at explicit resync; never retroactive. Changing the policy does not change any existing session's snapshot. A session's `fork_mode` and `policy_rev` are visible in `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/policy` and in `chd_whoami`. - **VOLD-062 (resync).** `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/policy-resync` requires `expected_policy_rev`, a `reason`, and an authorization (the agent's own session-policy authority or a `session.policy_resync` grant). It is an explicit operation only: when `session.resync.enabled=false`, it returns `403 policy_resync_disabled` and writes no snapshot. When enabled, it writes exactly one new snapshot revision, audits the change, and is atomic. Denial is `403 policy_resync_not_granted` (audited); stale revision is `409 policy_revision_conflict`. Resync may not widen beyond the agent's configured pool and is never automatic in preserve-parent mode. - **VOLD-063 (restore interaction; superseded by D-039).** A restored session retains the archived snapshot only as immutable history and **always resolves current permissions before activation**, whether or not the snapshot is present. The restore decision is `current_policy`; `snapshot_missing` records historical coverage only. The report records source/effective policy revisions, with a null source revision plus a verified reason when absent. Fork behavior remains separate: preserve-parent is the default and current-policy is an explicit authorized alternative.

## PART II — PROVISIONING AND LIFECYCLE (R31-020, R31-025)

## 2. Provisioning, profile lifecycle, and readiness (new)
Everything in this part is an operation with a card in `contracts/OPERATIONS.md`; this section fixes the content those cards must carry and the invariants they enforce.

### 2.1 The profile invariants
- **VOLD-064.** Every director, manager, supervisor, foreman and worker SHALL run under a distinct, non-default Hermes profile. The document is invalid if any two agents share `(instance, profile)` (`profile_shared`) or if any agent names the `default` profile (`profile_not_distinct`). A temporary worker gets a generated profile name and the same check applies. - **VOLD-065.** Profile identity maps 1:1 onto credentials and state: `agent → hermesBinding.instance (gateway) → hermesBinding.profile → profile credential/ session store / memory scope`. The gateway authenticates the profile; CHD never reuses one profile's token for another agent. Profile isolation is **not** a sandbox: it separates state and credentials, not host privileges (D-023 scope note). - **VOLD-066.** A worker dispatch request whose profile is absent, shared, or equal to the foreman's fails closed before any run record is created (`422 profile_not_distinct` / `profile_missing`).

### 2.2 Desired vs effective configuration, drift, and convergence
- **VOLD-067.** Each agent has a **desired** configuration (the operator/VP-owned document) and an **effective** configuration (what the running profile actually has: settings, model/context, tools, skills, assets). Readback returns both plus a `config_digest` and a `drifted: true|false` flag. Drift is computed against the profile's own reported state, not against a locally cached copy. - **VOLD-068.** Convergence is an operation (`chd_profile_sync`): it computes the diff, uploads changed assets, updates settings, and verifies by re-reading the effective state. It MUST NOT overwrite agent-learned memory or session history; it changes configuration and skill assets only, and it records what it replaced so a rollback is possible. - **VOLD-069.** Updates and rollback: `rollback_to_config_digest` restores the prior desired document and converges; the audit keeps both digests. A failed converge leaves the previous effective state intact and reports `converge_failed` — never a half-applied profile.

### 2.3 Asset packaging and transport (N-5 PROPOSED)
**VOLD-070a (managed composition):** The effective profile is composed in this order: project/workspace instructions, base-role template, named specialization, settings/tool policy, and provider/model/context runtime. The controller records desired and effective config revisions and their digests; Hermes owns behavior composition, while CHD owns the selected asset list and authorization boundaries.
**VOLD-070b (drift/readiness):** Drift is detected by comparing a profile's reported effective revision, settings, skills, tools, runtime and asset inventory against its desired revision. A profile is not ready when any digest or credential/readiness probe disagrees. Synchronization is update → asset upload → digest readback → smoke turn; failure retains the previous effective revision and emits `converge_failed`. No request may silently fall back to the `default` profile or another agent's profile.
**VOLD-070c (lineage):** Every update, rollback, default-profile migration, temporary-worker reuse/retirement and cleanup writes a central archive lineage record containing agent id, old/new profile, desired/effective revisions, asset digests, session archive refs and actor. Cleanup removes live state only after terminal run and archive checkpoint verification.
- **VOLD-070.** Skills, prompts and small assets are packaged as a content-addressed bundle (`manifest.json` + files, sha256 per file). Transport is **PROPOSED** (`asset.transport: "controller_upload" | "gateway_fetch"`); the default is controller upload with digest verification. A bundle whose digest does not match is refused. Large artifacts are referenced, not packaged. - **VOLD-071.** Verification after upload is a readback of the profile's asset inventory (name, version, digest). Presence alone is not verification.

### 2.5 Temporary workers: create, reuse, retire, cleanup
- **VOLD-074.** A temporary worker profile is created per work unit (or reused only within the same work unit), carries the same non-default invariant, and is retired after its run reaches a terminal state and its archive checkpoint is committed. Cleanup removes the profile's live state but MUST preserve the central archive records ([VOL-F replacement map](VOL-F-reference-map.md) (historical section 7)). Default values for lifetime/caps remain **OPEN-VOLD-1**; until ruled, a temporary worker is explicit-required (model, context, lifetime, workspace) and is unsupported if any is absent (`temporary_agents_unspecified`).

### 2.6 Retirement and offboarding
- **VOLD-075.** Retiring an agent: stop dispatch, drain or cancel its open sends (with recorded reasons), archive its sessions, revoke its credentials and grants, keep its records for retention, and mark the registry entry retired. A retired agent's history remains readable per its archive grants; its live profile and tokens are removed.

### 2.7 Readiness gates for provisioning
- **VOLD-076.** An agent is dispatchable only when: config valid; profile distinct; credentials present and probeable; assets verified; gateway reachable; scheduler trigger (if any) registered; `chd` durability verified. Each gate has a named failure code and the provisioning record shows the first failure. This gate set is a superset of the startup gates in §5.1 and never weakens them.

### 3.1.1 Report schema v2 (superseded, lineage)
Rev 1.1's schema v2 (`id, produced_by, send_id, request_ref, attempt, session_ref, status, content_ref, ts`, single free-form content) is **superseded by v3** and carried only for lineage and migration. A v2 report is read and upgraded in memory to v3 with `content.class: "free_form"` and `attempt_id` synthesized from `(send_id, attempt)`. No new v2 report is accepted.

### 3.1.2 Correlation and outcome semantics
- **VOLD-022 (correlation)** — `send_id` + `attempt_id` + `request_ref` + `session_ref` bind every report to exactly one send attempt and its request message. The verify loop resolves the send manifest, checks `request_ref` equals the manifest's request key and `attempt_id` equals the open attempt, and rejects on mismatch: `bad_report{reason: wrong_request}` or `bad_report{reason: attempt_mismatch}`. **A newer report for the wrong request cannot close work** — the required F-013 completion demonstration. - **VOLD-023 (`waiting_human` status, amended by R31-005)** — `waiting_human` is a first-class report status, distinct from `deferred` and from missing-reply silence (D-012). It requires `waiting_for_human = {question, gate_ref, asked_at, requested_by}`. A valid waiting report: (a) is NOT counted as a failure, (b) closes the **attempt** (VOLC-067) and creates the wait record, (c) is propagated upstream by the parent (supervisor → manager → director) as a `kind: status` notice in the parent room, and (d) leaves the **send** open; on recorded resolution a successor attempt is composed (W12). If the wait stays unresolved past `verify.wait_timeout_s` (EXPLICIT-DEFAULT 4× `verify.deadline_s`) the harness enters the **verify ladder at rung 2** for **visibility only** — it never approves, closes, resumes or expires the gate. The approval gate itself has no expiry; resolution always requires recorded approval evidence (VOLD-036). - **VOLD-024 (status semantics)** — `done` requires ≥1 artifact AND `criteria_results` covering every criterion in scope for this assignment (§3.6), plus a content variant matching the assignment's `required_content`; `deferred` requires `reason`; `blocked` requires `reason` naming the blocker and matches the blocked→escalated path of D-009/Q-004; `failed` is explicit failure (no artifact required); a report failing shape validation is `bad_report{reason: schema}`.

### 3.2 Trusted timestamp origin (R31-011)
- **VOLD-025 (freshness rule v3; supersedes CHD-3 / v2 wording).** The freshness comparison uses **harness-recorded** times, never agent-asserted client clocks: `dispatch_ts` is written by the send orchestrator when the gateway POST for this `attempt_id` is accepted; `ingest_ts` is the harness ingress time when the report carrier is accepted and durably persisted. Freshness is `ingest_ts >= dispatch_ts` for the **same** `(send_id, attempt_id, session_ref)` correlation. Agent `ts` and timestamps inside an attached artifact are narrative evidence only. A carrier that was never accepted does not exist for verification purposes. The old CHD-3 wording (`report.ts > request.timestamp`) is explicitly **superseded**, not an alternate implementation.
An accepted envelope may contain a stale attachment: that does not make the envelope stale; the attachment's own timestamp is evaluated only during director acceptance review. An attachment with a mismatched attempt/session is rejected as `bad_report{reason: attempt_mismatch}` or `bad_report{reason: wrong_request}` and cannot close work.

### 3.3 Late, duplicate, and wrong-request rules (precedence per VOLB-056)
- **VOLD-026 (single precedence; no overlap).** Send manifests record `config_digest`, `dispatch_ts`, `attempt_id`, `session_ref`, and terminal state. The verifier evaluates exactly one first-match row, in this order:
| First-match condition | Result | State change | |---|---|---| | Same `(send_id, attempt_id, session_ref, content_digest)` as an accepted report | **Exact replay**: return original response; dedupe; no write and no counter | none | | Same `(send_id, attempt_id)` with a different content digest while the send is open | **Second different report**: `409 report_already_posted`; record an audit event, not a report | none | | Same send is terminal (and it was not the exact replay above) | **Closed-work duplicate**: record `duplicate_ignored`, increment `duplicate_ignored_total`; no re-verification | none | | Send is open, correlation matches, and `ingest_ts >= dispatch_ts` but after `deadline_ts` | **Late valid result**: accept/link with `late_report=true`; it may close only still-open work. If escalation already made the send terminal, the prior row applies | may close open send | | Send is open but freshness or correlation fails | **Stale/wrong report**: `bad_report{reason: stale|attempt_mismatch|wrong_request}`; audit and enter the ladder | none |
This table is the sole duplicate/late/freshness precedence. A report arriving after a terminal transition is never a second report or a closure; it is the closed-work row unless it is an exact replay. A late result cannot reopen terminal work. A late report that would change an acceptance decision is material for director review and may be explicitly reopened only by an authorized change record (VOLD-033), never by arrival alone. - **VOLD-027** — Timer start points (all measured from harness-recorded times): the verify deadline starts at `dispatch_ts` (gateway POST accepted), not at composition and not at fire-callback receipt; reminder gaps are measured from the previous remind's dispatch; `waiting_human` pauses the deadline clock while the wait is authorized (VOLD-023). A queued send's staleness clock (`stale_after_s`) runs from composition, so a send cannot queue forever and then dispatch stale.

### 3.4 Rung transitions (ladder, per F-011/F-013)
- **VOLD-028** — Rung transitions are evaluated only at transition checks: rung 0 remind (REUSE, up to `max_reminds`, spaced `remind_gap_s`) → rung 1 fresh session (NEW) → rung 2 escalate. Each transition requires "still no valid report at the transition check" where *valid* means: arrived, schema-valid, fresh (VOLD-025/026), correlated to this send (VOLD-022), and not a `waiting_human` wait in force (VOLD-023). A missing *reply* (no message in the subthread and no attached work report — RL-11's mechanical detection) enters the same ladder at rung 0 with the dual action (notify caller + bump owing session); a missing *report* (reply or acknowledgment arrived, report did not) enters at rung 0 with only the bump leg. Both are counted distinctly (`missing_reply_total`, `reports_missing_total`) and no rung resets any counter. Reminder intervals are exactly `verify.remind_gap_s`; there are no exponential reminder retries inside a rung (backoff exists only in transport retry, §3.4).

### 3.5 Three layers of completion (F-013; D-010, D-012, Q-006)
- **VOLD-029** — Three distinct judgments, never conflated: 1. **Manager-reported completion** — a report with `status: done` for its send. Producer: the reporting agent. This closes the *send*, not the objective. 2. **Director acceptance review** — the director evaluates the report against the assignment's criteria record (§3.6), producing a structured acceptance verdict. Owner: the director (D-010: "after a manager reports completion, director starts acceptance review"). 3. **Objective acceptance** — the VP-facing state of the whole objective: all constituent sends verified, director acceptance recorded, any VP-conditioned delivery and human-approval conditions satisfied per the per-assignment rule (Q-006). Owner: recorded as the director's objective-level verdict delivered to the VP; where the VP's condition requires the human's acknowledgement, the condition text says so and the objective is not complete until the recorded evidence exists. - **VOLD-030 (objective state machine — canonical machine is VOL-A §4.1)** — The normative objective lifecycle is VOL-A §4.1's state table (VOL-A-025): `created → decomposing → assigned → in-progress` with `queued`/`blocked`/`escalated`/`awaiting-human` side states, then `in-acceptance → composing → delivering → accepted`, or `rework` back to `in-progress`, or `cancelled`. VOL-D's report/acceptance layer maps onto it as follows and introduces NO second machine: *manager_complete* = the entry condition of `in-acceptance` (all owner managers reported); *acceptance_review* = the `in-acceptance` activity; *rework*/*blocked*/ *cancelled* = the VOL-A states of the same names; *accepted_pending_ delivery* = `delivering` (separately delegated per D-011); *delivered/ objective_complete* = VOL-A `accepted` — reachable only when the VP-conditioned delivery segment applies and its delivery evidence (VOLD-031) is recorded. The delivery segment (`composing`/`delivering`) exists only when the VP's completion condition includes delivery. Every transition names its actor and stores its evidence key. Completion of a wake (a send closing) is never completion of the objective. - **VOLD-031 (content acceptance ≠ delivery success)** — Delivery is a separate stage (D-011): the delivering agent (director if equipped, or a delegated comms manager → supervisor per §1.6 grants) produces **delivery evidence**: `{channel, channel_message_id, delivered_at, delivery_attempt, idempotency_key}` recorded in the objective record. Delivery failure retries with the same `idempotency_key` (idempotent redelivery); delivery success is recorded as evidence only — it is *content acceptance* (director acceptance, and any human approval the VP conditioned on) that completes the objective, per the per-assignment condition of Q-006. A channel confirmation never substitutes for a required human approval.

### 3.6 Criteria: provenance, version, per-criterion evidence
- **VOLD-032** — Every acceptance criterion is a record: `{criterion_id, provenance: vp_supplied | director_derived | standing_rule, version, text, applies_to}`. - `vp_supplied` — arrived in the VP objective; immutable by the director (extension is additive only, D-010). - `director_derived` — created by the director when the VP supplied none, or added to cover additional requirements (D-010); provenance and creating-agent recorded. - `standing_rule` — resolved from Hermes-effective standing rules at acceptance time. - **VOLD-033 (carried unchanged)** — The director's completion and approval conditions flow into assignments verbatim; managers carry them to supervisors rather than replacing them (D-012). Any change to a carried condition requires an **authorized change record** `{changed_by, authority_ref, at, delta}` stored with the assignment; without one, a downstream report or agent asserting different conditions is `bad_report{reason: schema}` at review and the attempt is an integrity violation if it mutated stored state. - **VOLD-034 (standing-rule evidence, Q-005/D-013)** — Standing-rule integration belongs to Hermes's learning loop (D-013). CHD does not implement rule-update timing. What CHD requires and records: at acceptance review, the director cites the **effective-rule evidence** — the standing rules it could read at review time (with their Hermes source/versions as returned by Hermes readback) — and per-criterion `evidence_refs`. Because propagation to in-flight or future sessions is a Hermes dependency whose guarantees are unverified (review-log caveat: session-start frozen memory snapshots), acceptance records name the rule set actually consulted; absence of a newly announced rule from that set is recorded, not papered over. Conflicting rules and newly-changed-rule application to in-flight work remain owner-level: **OPEN-VOLD-3.**

### 3.7 Rejection and rework
- **VOLD-035** — A director rejection produces a structured rework record: `{objective_id, assignment, rejected_criteria: [criterion_id], reason, rework_scope, returned_to}` posted as a `kind: directive` reply in the owning thread (R-025 threading) and recorded in the objective record. Rejections preserve ownership and evidence: the reworked assignment references the original request/report keys, so artifact lineage survives (F-004 cross-ref: VOL-A owns the full lifecycle; this volume owns the verdict shapes).

### 3.8 Timeout is not permission; waiting states (D-012, Q-006)
- **VOLD-036** — Three states MUST remain distinct in every report, manifest, and objective record: - **missing reply** — mechanical: no subthread reply and no attached work report (RL-11) → ladder with notify+bump. - **missing report** — some traffic but no valid report → ladder, bump leg only. - **waiting-for-human** — explicit `waiting_human` report (VOLD-023) → no failure count, timer paused while authorized, propagated upstream. A timeout, an expiry, or a configured interval elapsing **never** grants an approval, closes an approval gate, or authorizes continuation. A wait timeout may only emit the bounded visibility escalation; it does not close the logical send, release an unproven run slot, or create a successor attempt. Continuation past a wait happens only when *prior human authorization* exists in the agent's `approval` configuration or a recorded VP authorization (D-012); an explicit stop-until-approval gate holds until the recorded approval evidence exists, regardless of elapsed time (Q-006). There is no universal delivery-versus-acknowledgement rule: the completion condition is per assignment (Q-006), carried unchanged per VOLD-033.

### 4.2 Bounded comparison and steady-state goal (R31-012)

The comparison unit is the **median cost of N identical unchanged cycles** vs the **median of the preceding N** (`N` = `measurement.window_cycles`, default 5), with a stated tolerance (`measurement.nonregression_tolerance_pct`, default 10). Pass = the later median ≤ earlier median × (1 + tolerance). The floor is a **zero-wake cycle** with cost 0; there is no requirement to go below it. A single cycle never carries a verdict. - **VOLD-081 (steady state).** The steady-state goal is a **band**, not a descending sequence: once the unchanged-cycle median falls inside `measurement.steady_state_band_tokens` and stays there across a full window, the target is met and no further reduction is required. - **VOLD-082 (cycle scope and boundaries).** A "cycle" is one director sync lane fire plus the sends it composes, bounded by the fire callback and closed when all its sends reach a terminal or waiting state. Startup, endpoint-driven wakes, user-triggered wakes and worker runs are **not** cycles and are reported separately. The 8-cycle figure is a pin-derived ceiling on **burn opportunities** (4 fires/day × 2 days), never a token target and never a universal law across deployments (VOLD-046 retained, restated). - **VOLD-083 (measurable startup and persistence).** Each measurement run records: the config digest, the fixture revision, the seed, the lane cadence, the raw per-cycle samples, and the counter snapshot before/after. Startup cost (harness start → first successful status) is measured separately and reported; counter persistence across restart is asserted by comparing snapshots.

### 5.2 Transport checks, restore ordering, queued-work recovery
- **VOLD-039** — Each transport (`loopback | tailscale | ssh-tunnel | direct`) has a named pre-dispatch reachability check owned by the gateway row; transports NEVER fail over silently (§5.2): a tailscale endpoint that is down fails loudly, it does not leak to a LAN route. Restore ordering after a partition or restart: (1) transport check passes → (2) mark gateway reachable → (3) resume queued sends **oldest-first**, preserving composition order → (4) re-arm ladder timers from their recorded deadlines (missed reminds are re-sent per current cadence, NOT burst-fired) → (5) `paused:unreachable` clears. No queued send is dropped by a restart; staleness (`stale_after_s`) is the only dropper and its clock continues across restarts. - **VOLD-089 (session-archive restore ordering — R31-016).** Restoring a session from the central archive (`chd-archive`) follows the ordered procedure VOLB-070 (VOL-B §5.10), and re-enters normal operation only after it: (1) replacement discovers the SessionArchive via the QA-1 lookup under a resolvable archive read grant (VOLC-081; no implicit read); (2) latest committed ExportManifest selected (QA-2) and its payload digest-verified; (3) **compatibility/version check** — `export_schema.name` must be `hermes.session.export` (probed, OPEN-6) at a version the importer supports, else the procedure stops `restore_failed{reason: export_version_unsupported}`; (4) import into a NEW local session store under a freshly minted session id; (5) policy snapshot imported, `snapshot_missing` failing closed to `current_policy` (VOLD-063); (6) new bond records the imported checkpoint; (7) restore report states completeness, coverage window and open gaps. **Limitation (normative):** archive restore CANNOT restore a live session — it is an import, never a resumption or a copy of a live database (VOLB-053).

### 5.3 Crier bridge lifecycle (RL-18, CT-15, FACT-32)
- **VOLD-040 (direction and conversion)** — - **Outbound:** a room event on a room configured `bridge: crier` is converted to a crier event envelope `{topic: <configured topic>, event: {delivery_id, room, seq, kind, payload}}`. Two destinations: crier **topic** (relay publish, fire-and-forget, dropped by crier on zero subscribers — hence not default) or crier agent **durable inbox** (default for anything that matters, per DESIGN §11.4). Topic publish is permitted only when the config explicitly selects it for that room. - **Inbound:** a leased crier inbox message becomes a room message `from: crier/<agent-id>` posted through the harness ingress (DESIGN.md §11.2) with the same VP auth and audit as any VP signal. Payload conversion is total: a message that cannot be converted is dead-lettered (recorded, counted `bridge_inbound_rejected_total`), never silently dropped and never partially posted. - **VOLD-041 (delivery ids, retry, ACK point)** — Every outbound bridge delivery carries a `delivery_id` used as the crier idempotency key; retries reuse it (idempotent redelivery). Outbound failures retry with exponential backoff, bounded, then dead-letter with a count and an incident message in the announce room (R-017: every escalation leaves a durable record). **The ACK point for inbound messages is after the room message write is durably committed** — given the F-019 correction, the bridge records WHICH durability mode it verified before ACKing; under buffered (non-barrier) durability the bridge MUST either configure a stronger mode for `chd` room keys or record `ack_mode: buffered` in the delivery record so the acknowledged-durability question is answerable (F-019 completion: "acknowledged durability matches configured/achieved mode"). Lease expiry with no ACK causes crier redelivery — safe, see loop prevention. - **VOLD-042 (loop prevention and outage isolation)** — Bridge-originated messages carry an origin tag (`via: chd-bridge/<bridge-id>`). The bridge never re-egresses a message that arrived inbound through the same bridge (no room→crier→room echo). A redelivered crier message whose `delivery_id` already has a committed room message is ACKed without a second room write (no duplicate room event). Crier outage: undeliverable bridge traffic is counted loudly (mirroring crier's error-notification shape), the announce room gets one incident per outage window (not per message), and nothing in the verify loop, ladder, caps, or rooms blocks on crier (CT-15).

**VOLD-085 (routing readback and no silent degradation).** The effective routing (VOLD-057) SHALL be readable per class and MUST match actual behaviour: `GET /v1/effective-routing` returns `{class, backend, namespace, sync, proxy, credential_ref_name, digest}`. A control write that would land on a delayed path is refused, not silently accepted. `project_code_memory` lag is recorded as `last_synced_rev/ts` and surfaced; a report's acknowledgement never depends on it.

### 5.5 Crier director federation (R31-029, D-035)
**VOLD-088 (federation operating story).** Crier federates **independent director systems**, often under different owners. The model is an owner-bounded trust contract, not room delivery with a larger ACK:
- Each side has its own VP, director, managers, supervisors, foremen and workers. A peer director is **not** an extra internal tier. Internal reinvocation of the same director (a new room/cycle) is distinct from an autonomous peer system; the former has local provenance and does not use the peer trust path. - **Identity/authentication/onboarding:** a peer is the configured principal `crier:<peer-id>`, authenticated by its configured mTLS public key or signed token. Operator onboarding writes a stable onboarding record naming peer id, key/token reference, owner label, expiry, allowed objective/message/room and ticket-family scopes, whether automatic requests are allowed or proposal-only, and the local approval route. Connectivity or a sender id alone confers no authority. - **Scope and grants:** a peer may use only explicitly configured scopes. A downstream grant must be an explicit GrantRecord with issuer lineage and may not exceed the local issuer's `grant_use`/`meta_grant` bound (VOL-C §8.3); peer trust never creates VP grants. Local VP configuration wins conflicts. - **Incoming direction mapping:**
| Incoming peer direction | Local actor | Required provenance / decision | |---|---|---| | signed peer objective request | mapped `peer:<peer-id>` actor | `origin=peer`, `peer_id`, `peer_request_id`; local VP scope check | | peer progress/message | mapped peer actor in configured room | `origin=peer`, `peer_message_id`, local room scope | | peer report/ack | mapped peer actor, report verifier | `origin=peer`, `peer_report_id`, correlated local ticket/send | | sender asserts `as: vp` | no VP mapping | refuse `403 peer_vp_claim`, audit; local VP precedence remains absolute |
The local VP is the only VP for local decisions. A remote sender never becomes local VP, even if its peer record is trusted or its message says `as: vp`. - **Approval and denial:** a permitted request is accepted only within configured scope; a proposal-only or approval-gated request is routed to `local_vp` (or configured local director/operator) and held as `202 pending_local_approval`. Untrusted, expired, malformed, or out-of-scope work is refused as `403 peer_scope_denied` (or `403 peer_authentication_failed` before scope evaluation), with no local objective, dispatch, or grant side effect. - **Correlated trace:** `peer_request_id=pr-42` arrives from peer `client-alpha`, maps to local actor `peer:client-alpha`, and passes local VP policy. The local director creates `objective_id=obj-local-42` and `ticket_id=ticket-42`, records ownership/acceptance in control state, assigns permitted work, and emits `peer_report_id=rr-42` carrying `peer_request_id`, ticket, report digest and acceptance. Retries reuse `peer_request_id`; duplicate requests replay the existing mapping and never create a second objective. - **Denial trace:** an untrusted `client-rogue` or a trusted peer asking for `room:private` reaches authentication/scope validation, is denied with `403 peer_scope_denied`, and produces only an audit record; no objective, dispatch, report, or grant is created. If configured for human review instead, the result is `202 pending_local_approval`, not autonomous work. - **Retry/outage/audit:** every request, reply, report, acceptance, denial, duplicate and approval decision is correlated and audited. Bridge outage stops federation traffic only; local work continues. Bounded retries are idempotent and dead-letter after their limit; no local ladder or completion status is changed by peer unavailability. - **Human examples** (two owners splitting a project; one owner coordinating several client directors) are illustrative, not a universal topology. Crier moves work, not DuckBrain project knowledge; project-memory federation is independently configured and drawn separately (D-035).
